tradition_assertions.notes: Reviewed work/title crosswalk: the Church's numbered list names Obadiah; TAU's index uses the Latin form Abdias, and the linked book-specific page identifies the Ethiopic Book of Obadiah. This matches the named biblical work only; Bachmann's 1892 critical edition transcription is not identified as a current EOTC printed edition and its text has not been freshly collated. British Library Add MS 16189's catalog lists the Twelve Prophets in this Ge'ez codex at folios 42v–64v and names a starting folio for each. This is manuscript-catalog evidence only; it does not verify a transcription, complete book boundaries, or identity with a particular current Church edition. Standard USFM title-candidate research readers are catalogued for Obadiah.

witness.title: Bachmann 1892 Ethiopic Obadiah critical edition; THEOT Project text transcription (2013), displayed by TAU
witness.date_statement: Printed critical edition 1892; THEOT transcription February 2013; TAU information page dated April 2010
witness.repository_or_publisher: Tel Aviv University website; Textual History of the Ethiopic Old Testament (THEOT) Project
witness.editorial_policy: The source transcription follows Bachmann's critical edition. The source page links verse labels to external navigation references; local extraction retains verse labels and raw HTML. Critical apparatus and facsimile images are not included.

coverage.structure_description: The captured TAU Text option is a single page with 21 sequential source-linked labels for chapter 1, verses 1–21. Complete for this locally captured digital Text page only; not a print-edition or manuscript completeness claim.
coverage.supplements_and_editorial_signs: HTML whitespace is normalized; source markers are stored separately; visible Ethiopic punctuation and signs remain. Raw HTML is retained. No critical apparatus or facsimile pages are included.
coverage.numbering_policy: Preserve the exact source labels 1–21 as strings and integer navigation numbers. They are the source page's labels, not a reviewed alignment to other textual witnesses.
